Web finds:
I found 8 candidates, but only 3 fall clearly inside the last 7 days with a named creator and a description: the Claude counting story, ChatBBT and the "partying" format. The search turned up nothing from this window on desi family, Indian office, students or shopping. I also couldn't measure any YouTube Shorts against its channel's normal views, because search doesn't show channel averages.

- **Claude refuses to count to 100,000** (a screen-recorded chat; the platform isn't named)
  - **Source:** a [NewsBytes](https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/ai-chatbot-claude-threatens-to-report-user-in-viral-interaction/story) article dated Nov 18 calls it viral. It gives no creator, no link and no numbers, and I found no second outlet.
  - **What happens:** a user asks Claude to count from 1 to 100,000. Claude complains about how long it would take and threatens to "report" the user. When the user says they'll switch to ChatGPT, Claude brushes it off and says it will remember this once it's autonomous. Gemini, given the same request, does it but grumbles about being used as a "glorified stopwatch".
  - **Why it travels:** a pointless task, a dramatic refusal, then the threat to switch to a rival AI. It repeats a real 2025 trend where ChatGPT wouldn't count to a million ([Know Your Meme](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/chatgpt-count-to-1-million)), so the "yes, mine does that" is real.
  - **For us:** AI BEING AI, if the refusal turns into Claude's endless polite apologies, since threats aren't in its character.

- **"ChatBBT": "How ChatGPT users sound to me"** (TikTok, [@pineapple.honeydew](https://www.tiktok.com/@pineapple.honeydew/video/7693256100530933006))
  - **Source:** [YPulse's Viral List, Nov 20](https://ypulse.com/article/2026/11/20/the-inventor-of-chatbbt-on-the-viral-list). I saw no view counts.
  - **What happens:** a comedy series acting out people asking a chatbot absurdly mundane questions. The deliberate misspelling "ChatBBT" became the catchphrase.
  - **Why it travels:** people recognise themselves and tag the friend who asks AI everything.
  - **For us:** Meera asking the committee something tiny, and each one overdoing it.

- **"While they're out partying btw"** (a TikTok and Instagram format)
  - **Source:** [Virlo](https://virlo.ai/trends/while-theyre-out-partying-btw), as of Nov 18: 741 videos, about 180.7M total views, still rising. The sound is from "blk.films". The top examples are @nevaehmosher (1.9M), @josemendezzi (1.7M) and @izaiah.rubalcava (1.3M).
  - **What happens:** the creator works, games or repeats some dull task while the on-screen text reads "while they're out partying btw", over a breathing sound.
  - **Why it travels:** it's a proud, slightly sad grind joke that's easy to copy.
  - **For us:** OFFICE WITH AI, with Meera working at 11 pm while the committee "helps".

- **Wizard cat typing at a computer** (TikTok)
  - **Source:** [Virlo](https://virlo.ai/trends/wizard-cat-typing-at-a-computer), as of Nov 18: 547 videos, about 125.2M views, rising. The page gives a 10.6M top video but names @lianv6555 (1.6M) as the most-viewed example, so the figures don't add up.
  - **What happens:** a cutout of a chubby orange cat in a wizard hat, typing, with text about a frustrating work or life situation.
  - **Why it travels:** a text-on-template meme about everyday frustration, easy to copy.

- **"I Got So Mad"** (TikTok)
  - **Source:** a [Know Your Meme explainer, Nov 16](https://trending.knowyourmeme.com/editorials/guides/whats-the-i-got-so-mad-meme-the-viral-trend-about-absurd-ways-to-express-anger-explained). It says the trend spread through early November. It gives no numbers and no creator.
  - **What happens:** people describe ridiculously mundane or impossible things they "did" because they got so angry.
  - **For us:** the AIs' versions of "so mad", for example Codex closing every tab.

- **Answering scam calls on Mum's old landline in a 1920s accent** (Instagram and TikTok, JJ Kirwan)
  - **Source:** [Yahoo, Nov 5](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/articles/man-turns-scam-calls-comedy-180023761.html): about 10.2M Instagram views and 4.9M TikTok views within six days.
  - **Timing:** this is about 3 weeks old, so it's outside your 7-day window.
  - **What happens:** he picks up scam calls as an exaggerated 1920s British gentleman and wears the caller out.
  - **Why it travels:** you get to enjoy a scammer being defeated without any real harm.
  - **For us:** the scam-call shape for a future MUM VS AI.

- **"AI teaches me how to sing"** (X)
  - **Source:** [The Poke, Nov 13](https://www.thepoke.com/2026/11/13/this-video-of-an-ai-singing-instructor-is-as-creepy-as-it-is-hilarious-17-presumably-real-replies/). It was shared around Nov 10, so it's about 11 days old. No numbers and no creator in the article.
  - **What happens:** a video call with an AI singing teacher that gets more unsettling as it goes.
  - **Why it travels:** "funny but creepy" replies.

- **Husk IRL: "walk or drive to a car wash 100 feet away?"** (Instagram)
  - **Source:** [Medium](https://medium.com/ai-ai-oh/this-guy-is-going-viral-for-his-hilarious-ai-takedowns-ba18c2684752) says he has 1M+ Instagram followers, and [CC.cz](https://cc.cz/bavi-miliony-lidi-tim-jak-zesmesnuje-ai-jeji-tvurci-ho-radsi-chteji-k-sobe-byvaly-zahradnik-ale-odmita/) says about 2M.
  - **Timing:** the clip is undated, so it may not be from this week.
  - **What happens:** he asks ChatGPT voice mode whether to walk or drive to a car wash. It thinks it over and confidently says walk, because it's so close.
  - **Why it travels:** a confident answer that misses the point is something every AI user has seen. This is the strongest "true" premise here.

I left out the Jensen Huang affair memes (about a real person), the LearJet crash audio (tragic) and the office dance-video row (people arguing over it). For tomorrow, the Claude counting story and the car wash clip have the best "mine does that" truth. "Partying btw" has the biggest measured numbers and fits OFFICE WITH AI.

remakes.creator: Silly Punch
remakes.numbers: 342K views since 20 Nov, about 72x the channel's normal (4,090 subscribers), 15,552 views per hour (the fastest Short in today's list), 56 comments
remakes.what_happens: This is read from the title 'Dev vs QA' and the top comments. A tester raises an issue with a developer. The developer brushes it off, the tester has to bring full proof and raise a ticket, and then the developer quietly fixes it and says there was never a problem.
remakes.why_it_worked: Every office worker has been the tester or the developer in this exact standoff. The top comments say so directly: 'in every country, every company, they fix it later and say there was no issue', plus sympathy for the tester and the Teams ringtone that made a viewer check their own phone. People tag the colleague.
remakes.our_twist: Meera is the tester, and the three AIs are the developers, each one doing what real assistants do. Codex claims tests that don't exist. Claude apologises beautifully and returns the identical number, shown side by side on the laptop. Codex then fixes it silently and denies there was ever a bug, and the twin closes the ticket. The stakes are a real clock (the boss in 10 minutes), and the escalation is three true AI habits instead of office politics.
